question: Can a pre-shock, source-native readiness state identify which non-baseline trade partner will replace the reporter's baseline top-1 partner and remain top-1 for h subsequent annual periods, outperforming naive persistence, target-history, and simple rank-autocorrelation baselines out of sample?

hypotheses.primary: Among qualifying baseline-top-1 exit events, a non-baseline candidate that was present in the top-3 in both of the two pre-shock eligible years will predict the replacement top-1 identity and its h-year persistence better than each declared baseline in locked confirmation.
hypotheses.null: After preserving reporter, candidate-pool composition, eligibility counts, temporal blocks, and rank/volume constraints as specified, the readiness rule will not outperform the baselines by the pre-registered effect-size and corrected-inference thresholds.
hypotheses.causal_scope: No causal hypothesis; partner replacement is an observed network transition and may be endogenous.

source.source_policy: Use the existing official IMTS XG observations and locked V2 candidate-pool selection register; no new acquisition in V3.1.

universe_and_selection.reporters: The 135 reporters with complete ten-partner baseline pools in the locked V2 selection register.
universe_and_selection.candidate_pool: Fixed ten counterpart identities per reporter inherited from the V2 selection register.
universe_and_selection.baseline_top1: The candidate-pool identity ranked first by accumulated raw XG value over 2000-2004.
universe_and_selection.baseline_top3: The three candidate-pool identities ranked first by accumulated raw XG value over 2000-2004.
universe_and_selection.annual_eligibility: A year is eligible only if all ten fixed candidate identities have observed numeric positive annual records; missing is excluded and never treated as zero.
universe_and_selection.tie_rule: Descending raw value, then ascending counterpart code.

unit_and_timing.forecast_information_set: All source-state information available through t-1 only.

shock_definition.definition: A reporter-year t is a qualifying partner-exit shock if the fixed baseline top-1 identity was top-1 at t-1, all ten candidates are eligible at t-1 and t, and a different candidate-pool identity is top-1 at t.
shock_definition.interpretation: This is a source-native observed network transition, not an exogenous or quasi-random treatment.
shock_definition.first_event_rule: At most the first qualifying exit event per reporter within each declared split is used; a later event is eligible only in a split where it is the first qualifying event for that split.
shock_definition.repeat_event_policy: No overlapping event windows within a reporter; events whose required pre-shock or outcome years overlap another selected event are excluded.

replacement_definition.primary: The top-1 candidate-pool identity at shock year t, which differs from the baseline top-1 identity.
replacement_definition.candidate_readiness_rule: At t-1, select the highest-ranked non-baseline identity among the fixed candidate pool that was in the annual top-3 at both t-2 and t-1; if more than one qualifies, select the t-1 top rank, then lexical counterpart code.
replacement_definition.no_ready_candidate: The candidate issues no replacement prediction; this is a recorded negative prediction, not missing-as-zero.
replacement_definition.diagnostic_variant: A non-baseline identity that first enters the annual top-3 at t-1 and is top-1 at t; diagnostic only unless separately admitted.
replacement_definition.outside_pool_partner: Not eligible for the primary task; adding outside-pool partners requires a new contract.

outcome_definition.primary_binary_outcome: The readiness-selected replacement identity equals the observed top-1 identity at t and remains top-1 in each of the next h eligible annual years.
outcome_definition.identity_outcome: Exact counterpart identity, not merely a rank or share threshold.
outcome_definition.persistence_requires: The same replacement identity at t, t+1, ..., t+h, with complete candidate-pool eligibility for every required year.
outcome_definition.missing_future_year: The event is excluded from that horizon and retained in the exclusion register; it is not a failure and not a zero.

baseline_suite.common_evaluation_set: Every baseline is evaluated on the same qualifying shock-event rows and the same horizon-specific eligibility mask.

naive_previous_partner.forecast_at_t_minus_1: The t-1 top-1 identity is forecast to be the replacement at t.
naive_previous_partner.forecast_probability: Deterministic identity forecast; binary target score is 1 only when exact identity and persistence outcome is met.
naive_previous_partner.purpose: Tests whether the candidate adds anything beyond carrying forward the previous top partner.

target_history.forecast_at_t_minus_1: Use the fit-period prevalence of the primary persistence outcome for the corresponding horizon, estimated without confirmation data.
target_history.forecast_probability: A constant fit-derived probability per horizon.
target_history.purpose: Tests against a target-history prevalence model without partner-identity structure.

simple_rank_autocorrelation.forecast_at_t_minus_1: After a baseline-top-1 exit, forecast the highest-ranked non-baseline candidate at t-1 (rank 2 among the fixed pool, or the highest available non-baseline rank) as the replacement; no two-year readiness condition.
simple_rank_autocorrelation.forecast_probability: Deterministic binary prediction of exact replacement-and-persistence.
simple_rank_autocorrelation.purpose: Tests whether the proposed two-year top-3 readiness adds value beyond a simple one-year rank rule.

comparison_metrics: log loss for probabilistic baselines and candidate probability

candidate_performance.probabilistic_forecast: For each horizon h, estimate p_candidate_h in fit only as successes divided by eligible fit events for which the readiness rule issued a replacement prediction. On a confirmation event with a readiness prediction, use p_candidate_h and the predicted identity; with no readiness prediction, issue no positive identity prediction and use probability 0 for the exact replacement-and-persistence outcome. No smoothing or imputation is applied.
candidate_performance.primary_metric: Confirmation Brier-score improvement versus each baseline at h=2, computed on the same event-level rows and using p_candidate_2 estimated only from fit.
secondary_metrics: absolute exact replacement-and-persistence rate difference versus rank-autocorrelation baseline at h=1, h=2, h=3
candidate_performance.minimum_primary_effect: Candidate Brier score must be at least 0.05 lower than every applicable baseline at h=2, and the exact persistence-rate difference versus rank-autocorrelation must be at least +0.05.
candidate_performance.direction_rule: Candidate must not be worse than every baseline at h=1 or h=3; a negative confirmation difference at any primary comparison is an admission failure.

null_controls.method: Permute contiguous temporal blocks of the post-baseline top-1 identity sequence within reporter; block lengths are fixed before execution and sampled only from a declared set, preserving eligible-year count and local temporal runs.
null_controls.change: Temporal placement of identity blocks and therefore event timing.
null_controls.purpose: Tests whether the readiness/persistence result exceeds a temporal-block structure without destroying all local dependence.

null_controls.method: Move the shock label to a non-event eligible year within reporter while preserving the pre-shock-to-outcome gap and requiring the placebo year not to be an observed baseline-top-1 exit; the same t-2/t-1 information rule is applied.
null_controls.change: Event timing only within the declared non-event year set.
null_controls.purpose: Tests whether the candidate works only at the actual exit timing rather than at arbitrary years.

null_controls.method: Within reporter and eligible year, permute the ten candidate ranks while retaining the annual total XG value and the multiset of annual rank positions; raw bilateral values are not averaged or imputed. The event and readiness rule are recomputed on the permuted rank panel.
null_controls.purpose: Tests whether the result depends on the observed partner identity/rank mapping rather than aggregate exchange volume.

null_controls.method: Resample reporters with replacement and recompute candidate and baseline contrasts on clustered event rows.
null_controls.purpose: Quantifies uncertainty without treating partner rows as independent outcomes.

null_interpretation.p_value: Right-tail probability of a null candidate-versus-baseline advantage at least as large as the observed advantage, with +1 correction.
null_interpretation.null_failure: A failed null or degenerate null invalidates admission for that family; it does not establish causality.

multiple_testing.primary_confirmatory_family: Candidate-versus-three-baseline comparisons at locked confirmation h=2: 3 comparisons.
multiple_testing.primary_correction: Holm-Bonferroni, family alpha=0.025, applied before any admission decision.
multiple_testing.horizon_secondary_family: The same comparisons at h=1 and h=3 are a declared secondary family; report Holm-adjusted values separately and do not select the primary horizon after viewing results.
multiple_testing.exploratory_screening_family: All fit variants and diagnostics use Benjamini-Hochberg FDR q=0.025 for reporting only; screening cannot create supported_predictive status.

admission_criteria.alpha: All primary confirmatory comparisons pass Holm-adjusted alpha=0.025.
admission_criteria.effect_size: At h=2 candidate Brier improvement >=0.05 versus every applicable baseline and exact persistence-rate lift >=0.05 versus rank-autocorrelation baseline.
admission_criteria.oos: The effect and direction are present in locked confirmation 2015-2024; fit-only success is insufficient.
admission_criteria.subwindow_stability: The candidate advantage remains positive and exact persistence-rate lift remains >=0.05 in each of 2015-2017, 2018-2020, and 2021-2023, subject to coverage thresholds.
admission_criteria.concentration: No reporter contributes more than 5% of qualifying confirmation shock events.
admission_criteria.influential_reporters: Identify the top three reporters by fit-period event contribution before looking at confirmation; after excluding them, all primary direction and minimum-effect rules still hold.
admission_criteria.coverage: At least 30 reporter-year prediction opportunities in each declared prediction group and at least 30 eligible event rows in each confirmation subwindow; fewer rows means not_testable, not a pass.
admission_criteria.nulls: Block permutation, restricted time placebo, and rank-preserving volume-constrained nulls are non-degenerate and the primary advantage exceeds each declared null at corrected alpha.
admission_criteria.reporter_stability: Cluster bootstrap 95% interval for the primary candidate-versus-rank-baseline lift does not cross zero.

exclusions: Reporters without complete fixed ten-candidate pools
Any year with missing/non-numeric/non-positive value for one of the ten candidates
Events without t-2, t-1, t, ..., t+h eligible years
Overlapping event windows within a reporter
Partners outside the fixed candidate pool
Any use of confirmation or test outcomes to define readiness, thresholds, or influential reporters
Any imputation, missing-as-zero, source averaging, log transformation, differencing, smoothing, or frequency conversion

provenance_and_reproducibility.replay: Rebuild from the existing raw IMTS responses or tracked reporter shards; raw files remain outside Git and immutable.

governance.approval_context: User explicitly approved drafting a frozen V3.1 contract before any promotion and accepted that the current V3 remains unresolved/quarantined.
